review_notes: I checked whether the aggregate `tprod_one_add`, which only takes `Summable (∏ i ∈ ·, f i)`, leaves out a caller who already knows the value (`HasSum (∏ i ∈ ·, f i) a`). It does not. The public `hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod` gives `HasProd (1 + f ·) a` directly, and `.tprod_eq` on that result gives the equation. In the submitted file, the other two lemmas (`multipliable_one_add_of_summable_prod` and `tprod_one_add`) are both proved through it. This is the same layout as the neighbouring Cauchy-product block: `HasSum.mul_eq` and `HasSum.mul` take convergence to a known value, and `Summable.tsum_mul_tsum` is the Summable-to-tsum version. So the triple HasSum→HasProd, Summable→Multipliable, Summable→tprod is complete, and an extra `tprod_one_add_of_hasSum` would only be a one-line restatement with no caller who needs it. The file has no bound lemmas (strict or non-strict), so that comparison does not apply. The hypotheses are minimal: the new section assumes only `[CommSemiring α] [TopologicalSpace α]`, adds `T2Space` only where `tprod_eq` needs it, and needs no `IsTopologicalSemiring` because the proof just composes with `tendsto_finset_powerset_atTop_atTop` after rewriting with `Finset.prod_one_add`. Some things are matters of taste and not defects, so I did not file them: proving `multipliable_one_add_of_summable_prod` as `(hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod h.hasSum).multipliable`, writing `(…).tprod_eq` instead of `HasProd.tprod_eq <| …`, changing the docstring wording to 'For a complete normed ring', and the explicit `Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset` import (harmless even if it is already pulled in transitively). The PR says only the Summable→Multipliable direction holds; that is correct for a general topological semiring, so leaving out an iff is right.
